questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I'm sorry, sir. / How many is / the fine for / returning the books late?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'How many is'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sentence **is related to the **present tense** where someone wants to know something.
 
• Here, the word '**fine**' is a **singular noun**, it **can't come** with the determiner '**many**'.
 
• **Much **is **accurate **with the word '**fine**'.
 
• The sentence should be *'I'm sorry, sir. **How much** is the fine for returning the books late?'*
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Let's understand the concept of **how much or how many.**

 
• **How much - **can be used with **an uncountable noun - sugar, time, money, milk, etc.** - ***How much time** will you take to get ready?*
 
• **How much - **can be used with** a countable noun to know the price - dress, jacket, etc. **- ***How much** is this **jacket**?*
 
• **How many - **can be used with** a countable plural noun - dresses, jackets, books, etc. **- ***How many dresses** have you bought?*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

He finally / recalled that / the thieves have leave / from the front door.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: ​**the thieves have leave**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is related to the verb tense.
 
• In this case, the present perfect tense "**have leave**" is incorrect.
 
• The **correct form should be in the past tense**, as the action of leaving occurred before the recalling in the past.
 
• The **correct phrase** should be "**the thieves had left**."
 
• **Corrected sentence**: *He finally recalled that the thieves had left from the front door.*
 
• In this corrected sentence, the past perfect tense "**had left**" is used to indicate that the thieves left before the main action of recalling took place.

Thus, **option 1** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.**

It turns out that my father isn’t alone.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **No error.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence has **no error. **
 
• The sentence is grammatically correct and follows the subject-verb agreement rule.
 
• **"My father"** is the subject and **"isn't alone"** is the verb phrase. The verb **"isn't"** agrees with the singular subject **"my father"**. 
 
 
• Example: She isn't alone in her struggle. (Subject: She, Verb: isn't alone)
 
 
 
• The phrase **"turns out"** is an idiomatic expression that is **commonly used to indicate a result or outcome that was unexpected, surprising, or contrary to what was initially believed or assumed.** It is often used to reveal new information or to share the realization of a particular fact or situation.
 
 
• Example sentence: "I thought I had lost my wallet, but it **turns out** it was in my backpack the whole time." (The result was contrary to the initial belief that the wallet was lost.)
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

She managed the company / so well that it is made / a huge profit that year.

options.text: so well that it is made

questions.solution:
The incorrect part is **'So well that it is made'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The usage of 'is made' is incorrect instead of this we need to use 'made'
 
• The given sentence is in the past tense as we can comprehend this from the very first verb of the sentence i.e. 'managed' so we need to use a past form of the verb in the other clause as well. So the correct verb form is 'made'
 
• The usage of 'so well that' is absolutely correct as so that is a correlative pair of conjunction that means 'with the purpose that; in order that'

**Hence, the correct sentence is-** *She managed the company so well that it** made** a huge profit that year.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.**

The integration of cutting - edge technologies into the healthcare industry __have the prospect__ of revolutionising the way medical professionals provide patient care.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "has the prospect."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence is in the present tense, so the verb should also be in the present tense.
 
• The error lies in the Subject Verb agreement.
 
• The subject "integration of cutting - edge technologies" is singular, so we need a singular helping verb** "has"** with it.
 
• **"Has the prospect" **means that there is a possibility or likelihood of something happening in the future, which fits the meaning of the sentence.
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

Correct sentence: *The integration of cutting - edge technologies into the healthcare industry has the prospect__ of revolutionising the way medical professionals provide patient care.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information​__*

 
• "Were the potential" is incorrect because "were" is past tense and does not match the present tense of the rest of the sentence.
 
• "Have the potential" is grammatically correct, but "has the prospect" is a better fit in terms of meaning.
 
• **"Will have potential"** is incorrect because it changes the meaning of the sentence to suggest that the potential is not currently present, but will be in the future.

questions.question:
Identify the error in the following sentence and select the option with the correct use of the phrasal verb.

Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he blacked out.

options.text: Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he turned down.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he checked out.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he chickened out.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he broke in.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the phrasal verb **"blacked out."**
 
• **"Blacked out"** means to lose consciousness, which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• The correct phrasal verb should be **"chickened out,**" which means to lose courage or decide not to do something out of fear.
 
• Thus, the error is located in the last part of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he **chickened out**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "turned down"** – This means to reject something, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 2: "checked out"** – This means to leave or depart, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 4: "broke in"** – This means to enter by force, which does not fit the context.

**In option 3**, the usage of **'Scientist have'** is incorrect instead use **'Scientists have'**

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Since childhood, Monty / ate his food / fast and he / will not change.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb tense in the fourth part of the sentence, 'ate his food', is incorrect.
 
• The sentence describes an ongoing characteristic from childhood to the** present, so the present perfect tense should be used.**
 
• The correct form should be **'has eaten his food'** to indicate the action started in the past and continues to the present.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4)

Correct sentence: *Since childhood, Monty **has eaten his food** fast and he will not change*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When describing actions or states that began in the past and continue to the present, the present perfect tense is used.
 
 
• **Example:** *She **has lived** in New York since 2010*.
 
 
 
• The present perfect is formed using **'has/have + past participle'** of the verb.
 
 
• Example: *They **have finished** their homework*.

options.text: his brother Peter’s newspaper The Morning Chronical

the tender age of nineteen when he joined

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**as journalist.**"

• The phrase "**as journalist**" is not a complete sentence and does not have a subject.
 
• A complete sentence would be "**as a journalist**" or "**as the journalist**."
 
• In the context of the sentence, "**as a journalist**" specifies the role or profession that Washington Irving assumed when he joined his brother Peter's newspaper.
 
• It's a grammatical convention to use the indefinite article in such constructions

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Corrected sentence**: *Washington Irving’s writing career started at the tender age of nineteen when he joined his brother Peter’s newspaper, The Morning Chronicle, as a journalist.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Hard had she / thrown the basketball / when it fell / on the ground.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘4’ i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the fourth part of the given sentence, the phrase 'Hard had she' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the correct phrase should be **'Hardly had she'.**
 
• This is a case of using an adverbial phrase in inversion to emphasize an action that just happened before something else.
 
 
• **Example:** ***Hardly had she** entered the room when the phone rang.*
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *Hardly had she thrown the basketball when it fell on the ground.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** *Hardly had they finished their meal when the waiter brought the bill.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

When Mayank came, / I shall go / with him to / the circus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **When Mayank came**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error in the original sentence is in the **verb tense agreement**.
 
• The issue is that the past tense "**came**" in this segment conflicts with the use of the future tense "**shall go**" in the following segment.
 
• In this case, "**comes**" is appropriate.
 
• This suggests that whenever "**Mayank comes**" as a regular occurrence or in the future.
 
• In conditional statements, especially those **expressing future conditions**, use "**comes**" in the **if-clause** to indicate a possible future event.
 
• So, the **correct sentence** would be: *When Mayank comes, I shall go with him to the circus.*

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I am going / to buy a red car / with a leather seats / and a sunroof.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the** third** part of the given sentence, the article 'a' is incorrectly used before the plural noun **'seats'.**
 
• In English grammar, the article** 'a'** is used before** singular countable nouns, whereas 'seats' is a plural noun.**
 
• The correct phrase should be** 'with leather seats'__ without the article 'a'.**

Hence, the correct statement is:** *I am going to buy a red car with leather seats and a sunroof*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When using articles before nouns, ensure that the article agrees in number with the noun it modifies.
 
 
• **Example:** *A book (singular) but books (plural) without 'a'*.
 
 
 
• Articles 'a' and 'an' are used with singular countable nouns, whereas 'the' can be used with both singular and plural nouns.
 
 
• Example: *The book (singular) and the books (plural) are on the table*.

• In conditional sentences, the word **'if'** is followed by the present tense to refer to the future.

• Therefore, the correct phrase should be **'rains'.**
